当然，弃子本身不等于高明，反对常识也不自动产生新知识。真正的区别，在于放弃一个前提之后，能不能解释原来解释不了的现象，能不能构造原来构造不出的东西，又能不能在实际使用中取得更好的结果。

但棋子与人还有一个根本区别：棋手可以按棋规决定自己的棋子怎样走，却不能因此推论，少数决策者有权为了一个自称更好的未来，替其他人决定牺牲生命或基本权利。把这个比喻用于制度设计，是鼓励我们重新考察假设、选择自己愿意承担的成本，并寻找减少共同损失的新路径。

changes.before: 知识可以被许多个体共同使用，而产生和使用这些知识的组织，其结构和运行机制却有很大差别。生物层面的大脑依靠大量不同神经元之间的连接和反馈形成能力，并没有一个单独的神经元以自己的身份永久支配一切。而人类社会的个体所形成的社会网络是一种更加静态的金字塔结构，所占有的资源和拥有的权力，以及决策的权重大小与在金字塔中的位置有关，且相对固定，缺乏即时的动态调整，比如一个能力超强的企业家或政治家，随着衰老过程伴随的认知和决策能力下降，但是其决策权重并不会因此就能快速的由更年富力强决策能力更强的新生代取代，而且金字塔结构下不同个体之间的相互博弈，在权力和资源的不对等的情况下，容易导致资源的低效分布和浪费。

changes.before: 奖惩机制其实就是一个评价函数，而以牙还牙策略，则是这个函数的迭代过程，它可以使关系在反复互动中加强或减弱，形成有方向的反馈，在相应条件下，可以让符合评价函数的结构趋于收敛，或让不符合评价函数的结构趋于分离，而不是随机的结合和分离，无法形成稳定的结构。而不同强度的以牙还牙策略，会影响不动点结构的收敛速度和结构强度和稳定性。强大的结构强度和稳定性会让不动点非常稳定强大，但是却容易陷入局部最优的不动点无法自拔，削弱甚至丧失了进化的能力。当然过于脆弱的结构稳定性也是不行的。所以如何构造一个合理的奖惩机制和收敛/发散策略的博弈策略，是影响整个人类文明进化能力的重要问题。
changes.after: 在一个简化模型中，可以把奖惩机制看作评价的一部分，把反复的互惠回应看作持续反馈的过程。它可以使关系在互动中加强或减弱，在相应条件下形成比较稳定的合作结构；也可能因为误判、过强的回应或条件变化而振荡、瓦解，甚至使参与者退出。以牙还牙是一种具体策略，并不等于任意评价函数的迭代，更不能仅凭“不动点”这个词就断言社会一定收敛。不同强度的回应，会影响关系的稳定性和修复空间。过强的结构稳定性可能使既有关系难以改变，削弱进化的能力；过于脆弱的关系也难以维持合作。所以，如何构造合理的反馈、奖惩与修复机制，使稳定和改变能够相互支持，是影响整个人类文明进化能力的重要问题。
changes.rationale: Remove the unsupported fixed-point convergence shortcut and agree with the later game-theory definitions.
changes.attribution: Author-requested editorial integration; baseline wording retains prior provenance; additions are not automatically author-approved.

这种借鉴首先是一种功能上的比较。人的大脑、Transformer和人类社会具有不同的结构、学习过程与权利关系。我们要从中提炼可以构造和检验的机制，而不是把其中一套术语贴到另一套系统上，就认为已经完成了设计。

我设想，让属于每个人类个体的根AI agent，也就是个人的super agent，映射出一个覆盖个体及其私有资源的个人空间。个人通过自己的大脑智能与自己的super agent协同，构造属于自己的注意力机制，进行自我管理和自我进化。上面的这些个体空间和个体智能，又一起参与构成更大的文明空间，在共同事务的层面上建立相应的注意力与协作机制。

changes.after:
Merkle-DAG可以保存这些变化的依据和版本。设备的身份与设备状态的版本需要分开：容量改变以后仍然是同一台设备，旧状态不能被悄悄覆盖为新状态；设备报废以后，历史记录仍然存在，但不能继续被列为当前可用资源。采集、推断、方案、授权、执行和结果，也要留下彼此的关系。哈希能够帮助核验内容与版本，现实是否确实如此、权限是否仍有效，还需要另外核查。

这与前面区分对象版本、运行环境和实际执行的思路相接。不可变的是某一份已经形成的记录，不是被记录的世界；需要持续更新的是我们对当前状态、承诺与权限的认识。运行时允许新对象和新规则进入，而历史记录保留这些变化怎样发生，两者共同构成可以学习的系统。

changes.after:
### 技术红利为什么没有自动变成共同幸福

一个令人触目惊心的事实，是技术改变世界的速度，与人类调整自身合作规则的速度之间，存在着巨大的落差。自二战以来，仅仅信息技术，就已经历经了计算机、集成电路、移动通信、互联网和AI的浪潮。人们收集信息、组织生产、传递知识和采取行动的能力，已经与几十年前不可同日而语。

当然，不能因此说，同一时期全球各国之间的政治、经济、金融博弈规则，各国内部的政治经济体制，几乎没有发生本质变化。去殖民化、福利与市场制度的调整、中国的改革开放、苏联解体以及国际货币体系的变化，都改变了大量人的生活。真正需要追问的是：在这些重大变化之后，许多组织中资源占有、信息控制和决策权力相互加强的基本关系，为什么仍然延续？当技术已经把一项决定的作用范围和传播速度放大许多倍时，受影响的人理解、参与、约束和纠正这项决定的能力，是否也得到了相应提高？我所说的制度落后，要在这种具体的不匹配中考察，不能只靠把过去几十年说成完全静止来成立。

尤其是从七十年代末以来的计算机信息时代，技术与生产的发展创造了大量财富，但财富增长并没有自动带来公平的分配。世界银行的一项估计显示，1995—2020年，全球实际人均综合财富增加了21%；这里包括生产资本、人力资本、自然资本和净国外资产，并不等于每个家庭可以支配的存款和财产，也不意味着所有国家都同步改善。[世界银行《国家财富的变化2024》](https://www.worldbank.org/en/publication/the-changing-wealth-of-nations)

与此同时，在一些重要经济体中，财富向顶端集中的程度明显提高。Saez和Zucman的一项研究估计，美国最富0.1%的家庭拥有的财富份额，从1978年的约7%上升到2012年的约22%，增至原来的三倍左右。中国的另一组历史估计显示，最富1%的人群所占财富份额，从1995年的约15%上升到2015年的约30%。这两组数据采用的顶端人群范围和年份不同，不能合写成“中美最富0.1%的财富份额都翻了三倍”，更不能把这些历史估计直接当成今天的数值。它们所提示的是：生产能力提高与财富分配改善，是需要分别考察的两件事。[美国财富集中研究](https://eml.berkeley.edu/~saez/SaezZucman2015.pdf)、[《世界不平等报告2018》](https://wir2018.wid.world/executive-summary.html)

这种落差也会表现为人们对公共生活的感受。在一些国家，民意割裂、排斥性的民族主义动员，以及对政府和经济处境的不满，成为反复出现的问题；国际间也依旧冲突不断。不能把这些不同的问题都归为一个原因，但它们至少提醒我们：拥有更多技术和财富，不足以保证形成更值得信任的共同生活。OECD在2023年对30个成员国开展的调查中，对本国政府表示低度或没有信任的受访者占44%，表示高度或中度信任的占39%。这是特定国家和时期的调查，并不代表全世界，更不等于所有公共服务都失去了信任。[OECD政府信任调查说明](https://www.oecd.org/en/about/news/press-releases/2024/07/governments-must-better-engage-all-citizens-to-tackle-growing-gaps-in-trust.html)

在个人层面，我想区分两种容易被混在一起的改善。一种是客观的“生存幸福”：食物、住房、医疗、教育和工具等生活条件得到改善；另一种是主观的“心理幸福感”：一个人是否安心，是否能够安排自己的生活，是否相信自己的努力有意义，是否在合作中得到尊重。这里是为了说明问题而作的区分，不是两项已经统一定义的统计指标。技术红利与公共制度的建设，可以使前一种条件增强；但如果分配、参与和纠错机制没有相应改善，后一种感受并不必然一起提高。

这也不能被说成全世界普通人、尤其是年轻人都在经历同一种集体滑坡。《世界幸福报告2026》指出，与较早时期相比，美国、加拿大、澳大利亚、新西兰以及西欧的青年生活评价出现下降，但其他地区并不呈现相同的总体图景。地区差异本身就是需要解释的材料：生活成本、就业与发展机会、家庭和社会关系、公共服务以及数字媒介，可能通过不同路径影响人的处境。不能从一条幸福感趋势，直接断言已经证明了某一种制度解释。[《世界幸福报告2026》执行摘要](https://www.worldhappiness.report/ed/2026/executive-summary-happiness-and-social-media/)

信息时代又附加了“坏事传千里”的放大效应。一个远处的冲突，可以立即进入无数人的日常生活；如果平台不断把最能刺激点击的内容推到眼前，人们感受到的世界就可能更加紧张。一项针对在线新闻标题的随机实验研究发现，负面措辞会提高点击率。它说明注意力竞争中的一种激励，并不能单独证明负面新闻造成了普遍的心理健康下降。[负面措辞与在线新闻消费研究](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41562-023-01538-4)

这也使前面关于注意力架构的讨论，有了一个非常具体的制度问题。同样是在分配注意力，究竟是优先让人停留更久、点击更多，还是帮助人理解与自己有关的真实问题，并获得解决问题的能力？能够准确预测一个人会点击什么，不等于已经理解什么对他的长期生活更有帮助。新机制不能仅仅把推荐算法做得更聪明，还要让本人能够参与决定目标、看见选择依据、调整或退出这种安排。与此同时，减少无谓的恐惧，并不意味着隐藏真实的坏消息；事故、侵害和失败仍然需要被看见，才能进入共同修复。

所以，我所担心的，并不是技术本身让人不幸福，而是技术带来的生产能力、信息能力和行动能力，未能通过相应的制度安排，充分转化为公平的发展条件、可靠的合作与个人能够掌握的生活。如果任由技术发展和制度变革之间的巨大速度落差再继续扩大下去，不稳定因素就可能逐步累积，从量变走向质变，增加严重冲突或危机的风险。危机会不会发生、以什么形式发生，仍取决于人们怎样回应。我们应当争取的，是在伤害尚可避免时就改进合作与纠错的机制，而不是等到危机爆发，再用更大的代价来迫使制度改变。

### 制度落差的判断，怎样接受事实检验

财富集中、政府信任与青年幸福感的资料，使我所担心的问题有了可以继续追问的经验入口；它们还不能合起来充当“旧制度必然造成所有问题、新制度必然解决所有问题”的证明。财富的总量与分配份额、收入与资产、最富0.1%与最富1%、不同年份与不同地区，都需要分开。全球平均值不能代替每一个人的处境，一些地区的恶化也不能代替全世界的趋势。关于负面措辞的点击实验，检验的是点击行为，不能直接替代对长期心理健康的研究。

“制度发展慢于技术”也需要从比喻变成具体问题。两者没有一把可以直接比较速度的共同尺子。可以在一项服务、一个组织或一个公共决策中，分别观察技术扩大了多少影响范围、错误传播得多快，以及受影响的人需要多久才能发现问题、提出异议、停止损害并完成修复。若治理改进能够缩短后一条链条，而没有以牺牲基本权利或把成本推给弱者为代价，就构成了与本书目标相关的进展。

进一步研究时，还需要比较不同的分配与治理安排，考察生活条件、可支配时间、真实参与、信任和主观生活评价怎样变化，并区分技术、公共政策、人口结构和其他条件的作用。实际结果如果表明某一种旧有安排在相同任务中更可靠，或新的注意力与权重系统只是提高了点击率、上传量和表面赞同，却没有改善人的生活，就应当据此修改方案。反过来，新的合作即使提高了满意度，也仍要检查它是否遗漏了退出者、沉默者和承担隐性成本的人。一个希望能够自我进化的文明机制，也必须允许事实修正它对自身优越性的判断。

changes.after:
A sacrifice, of course, is not intelligent merely because it is a sacrifice. Defying common sense does not automatically produce knowledge. The real question is whether relinquishing an assumption allows us to explain something previously unexplained, construct something previously unattainable, or achieve better results in practice.

There is also a fundamental difference between pieces and people. A player may move their pieces under the rules of chess; this does not entitle a few decision-makers to sacrifice other people's lives or basic rights for a supposedly better future. Applied to institutions, the analogy invites us to reconsider assumptions, choose costs we are willing to bear ourselves, and find paths that reduce shared losses.
changes.rationale: Connect the opening sacrifice metaphor to the later Watchmen argument without authorizing sacrifices imposed on others.
changes.attribution: Author-requested editorial integration; baseline wording retains prior provenance; additions are not automatically author-approved.

changes.before: Knowledge can be shared by many individuals, but the organizations that create and use it vary enormously. A biological brain acquires its capabilities through connections and feedback among many neurons. No single neuron holds permanent personal authority over the whole. Human organizations, by contrast, often arrange social networks into relatively fixed pyramids. Resources, power, and decision-making influence depend heavily on a person's position. An exceptional entrepreneur or political leader may lose some cognitive capacity with age, while retaining authority that does not readily pass to someone now better able to exercise it. Repeated interaction under unequal power and resource conditions can also produce waste and poor allocation.
changes.after: Knowledge can be shared by many people, yet the organizations that create and use it differ greatly. A brain develops capabilities through connections and feedback among neurons; many human organizations attach resources, authority, and influence to relatively fixed positions. How can shared knowledge and feedback actually change collective decisions, rather than leave everyone waiting for a few people in authority to change their minds? This is one of the questions the book will develop.
changes.rationale: Keep the detailed aging-leader example in the material-conditions chapter; give the preface its introductory role.
changes.attribution: Author-requested editorial integration; baseline wording retains prior provenance; additions are not automatically author-approved.

changes.before: An AI architecture could experiment with a persistent context for reflection, selecting material from conversations and observations in light of its current questions, and initiating further inquiry. A problem encountered while reading would not disappear at the end of a chat. It could remain a thread to revisit when new evidence arrives. The system might connect the evidence, reassess a judgment, or propose an experiment capable of distinguishing alternatives. Input would then contribute to a continuing activity rather than trigger an isolated reply.
changes.after:
An AI architecture could experiment with a persistent context for reflection, selecting material from conversations and observations in light of its current questions, and initiating further inquiry. A problem encountered while reading would not disappear at the end of a chat. It could remain a thread to revisit when new evidence arrives. The system might connect the evidence, reassess a judgment, or propose an experiment capable of distinguishing alternatives. Input would then contribute to a continuing activity rather than trigger an isolated reply.

Here, a unified context means the personal memories and tasks this agent is authorized to use. It does not mean collecting everyone's internal conversations into a central model. Personal agents can exchange permitted information for a shared task while retaining separate private spaces. Continuing personal reflection and cooperation across civilization are connected but distinct levels.
changes.rationale: Clarify the scope of global context and preserve the personal/shared distinction used by the attention architecture.

changes.before: Within either setting, differences can still appear around difficult or borderline cases. Broadly conciliatory participants may divide into harder and softer positions; even an authoritarian system can contain competing hawkish and dovish approaches. These possibilities are reasons to investigate the interaction of dispositions and institutions, rather than infer an entire social order from either alone.
changes.after: People do not respond identically even within the same institutions. Physiology, experience, position, and interpretation can differ. At a difficult threshold, participants who usually favor conciliatory methods may divide into harder and softer positions; highly centralized systems can also contain hawkish and dovish approaches to a particular issue. Whether and how genetic factors contribute requires specific investigation. Neither an institutional label nor a genotype determines in advance how a person will act.

changes.before: Rewards and penalties can be viewed as an evaluative mechanism; repeated reciprocal responses apply that mechanism over time. Under suitable conditions, relationships strengthen or separate in patterned ways. The intensity of responses affects convergence, resilience, and stability. Too much rigidity can trap a system in a local optimum and undermine its capacity to evolve; too little stability can prevent sustained cooperation. Designing feedback that supports both persistence and change is a central problem for civilization.
changes.after: In a simplified model, rewards and penalties can form part of an evaluation process, while repeated reciprocal responses provide feedback. Relationships may strengthen or weaken and, under suitable conditions, sustain cooperation. Misjudgment, excessive responses, or changing circumstances may instead cause oscillation, breakdown, or withdrawal. Tit for Tat is a particular strategy, not the iteration of any arbitrary evaluation function; invoking a fixed point does not prove social convergence. The strength of a response affects both stability and the room for repair. Excessive rigidity can obstruct change, while fragile relationships may fail to sustain cooperation. Designing feedback, incentives, and repair so that persistence and change support each other is therefore a central problem for civilization.

changes.after:
### Why technological gains do not automatically become shared well-being

One alarming feature of our age is the gap between the speed at which technology changes the world and the speed at which we revise the rules of cooperation. Since the Second World War, information technology alone has brought successive waves of computers, integrated circuits, mobile communications, the internet, and AI. Our ability to gather information, organize production, share knowledge, and act bears little resemblance to what it was a few decades ago.

That does not mean political, economic, and financial institutions have stood still. Decolonization, changes to welfare and market institutions, China's reforms, the dissolution of the Soviet Union, and changes to the international monetary system have transformed many lives. The harder question is why, after such changes, ownership of resources, control of information, and decision-making power still reinforce one another in so many organizations. Technology may multiply the reach and speed of a decision. Have the people affected gained comparable powers to understand it, participate in it, constrain it, or correct it? This is the institutional mismatch I want to examine. The argument does not require us to pretend that recent history was motionless.

The computer and information age, particularly since the late 1970s, has helped create enormous wealth. Growth, however, does not distribute its gains fairly by itself. The World Bank estimates that global real comprehensive wealth per person rose by 21 percent between 1995 and 2020. This measure includes produced, human, and natural capital, as well as net foreign assets; it is not a measure of the money and property available to each household, nor did every country improve together. [The Changing Wealth of Nations 2024](https://www.worldbank.org/en/publication/the-changing-wealth-of-nations)

Meanwhile, wealth became more concentrated at the top in some major economies. Saez and Zucman estimated that the share held by the wealthiest 0.1 percent of US families rose from about 7 percent in 1978 to about 22 percent in 2012—roughly three times its earlier level. A separate historical estimate for China put the top 1 percent's share at about 15 percent in 1995 and 30 percent in 2015. These figures concern different groups and periods. They do not establish that the top 0.1 percent's share tripled in both countries, and they are not estimates for today. They illustrate why productive capacity and the distribution of wealth must be examined separately. [US wealth concentration study](https://eml.berkeley.edu/~saez/SaezZucman2015.pdf), [World Inequality Report 2018](https://wir2018.wid.world/executive-summary.html)

The gap also appears in public life. Political polarization, exclusionary nationalist appeals, and dissatisfaction with government and economic circumstances recur in some countries, while international conflict persists. These problems have different causes, but they remind us that greater wealth and technical power do not guarantee a more trustworthy shared life. In the OECD's 2023 survey across 30 member countries, 44 percent of respondents reported low or no trust in their national government, compared with 39 percent reporting high or moderately high trust. This is evidence from particular countries and a particular period, not a verdict on the whole world or on every public service. [OECD explanation of its trust survey](https://www.oecd.org/en/about/news/press-releases/2024/07/governments-must-better-engage-all-citizens-to-tackle-growing-gaps-in-trust.html)

At the personal level, I want to distinguish two forms of improvement that are easily conflated. One concerns the material conditions of a good life: food, housing, health care, education, and useful tools. The other concerns how that life feels: whether we feel secure, can shape our days, find meaning in our efforts, and receive respect in cooperation. This is a distinction for developing the argument, not a pair of standardized statistical measures. Technological gains and public institutions can improve the first without ensuring that the second keeps pace, especially when distribution, participation, and correction remain inadequate.

Nor should this be described as a universal collapse in well-being among ordinary people or the young. The World Happiness Report 2026 identifies declining youth life evaluations in the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and Western Europe relative to earlier periods; other regions do not show the same overall pattern. That variation needs explanation. Living costs, opportunities, relationships, public services, and digital media may affect people through different pathways. A trend in reported happiness cannot, by itself, establish one institutional explanation. [World Happiness Report 2026 executive summary](https://www.worldhappiness.report/ed/2026/executive-summary-happiness-and-social-media/)

The information age adds another effect: bad news travels far and fast. A distant conflict can immediately enter millions of daily lives. When platforms repeatedly favor material that provokes clicks, the world people encounter may feel more threatening. A study of randomized online news headline experiments found that negative wording increased click-through rates. That identifies an incentive within competition for attention; it does not, on its own, prove that negative news causes a general decline in mental health. [Research on negative wording and online news consumption](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41562-023-01538-4)

This gives the earlier discussion of attention a concrete institutional purpose. When a system directs attention, is it trying to keep people watching and clicking, or to help them understand real problems and gain the ability to address them? Predicting what someone will click is not the same as knowing what will help them live well over time. A new system needs more than a cleverer recommendation algorithm. People must be able to help determine its aims, inspect its grounds, change its settings, or leave. Reducing needless fear must also not become an excuse to hide real bad news. Accidents, abuse, and failures have to remain visible if they are to be repaired.

My concern, then, is that our growing powers to produce, inform, and act may fail to become fair opportunities, dependable cooperation, and lives people can meaningfully direct. If the gap between technological change and institutional adaptation keeps widening, pressures may accumulate until they produce a serious conflict or crisis. Whether that happens, and what form it takes, still depends on how people respond. We should improve cooperation and correction while harm can still be prevented, rather than wait for a crisis to force change at a much higher cost.
changes.rationale: Place the new author-led evidence and argument between existing technological power and prospective AI acceleration.

### Testing the claim of an institutional gap

Evidence about wealth concentration, trust in government, and young people's well-being gives us concrete questions to investigate. Taken together, it does not prove that existing institutions necessarily cause every problem or that the proposed system will solve them all. Total wealth must be distinguished from shares of wealth, income from assets, the top 0.1 percent from the top 1 percent, and one period or region from another. A global average cannot describe everyone's circumstances; deterioration in some places cannot stand for a worldwide trend. Experiments on negative headlines measure clicking behavior, not long-term mental health.

The claim that institutions lag behind technology also needs to become more precise. There is no common ruler with which to measure their respective speeds. For a particular service, organization, or public decision, we can instead examine how technology expands the reach of an action and accelerates the spread of an error. We can then ask how long affected people need to discover the problem, raise an objection, stop the harm, and secure a remedy. Shortening that second chain without sacrificing basic rights or shifting costs onto weaker participants would be progress relevant to this book's aims.

Further research should compare arrangements for distribution and governance, examining material conditions, discretionary time, meaningful participation, trust, and people's evaluations of their own lives. It must distinguish the effects of technology, public policy, demographics, and other circumstances. If an existing arrangement proves more reliable for the same task, or if a new attention and weighting system merely increases clicks, uploads, and apparent agreement without improving lives, the proposal should change. Even higher reported satisfaction requires us to look for people who left, remained silent, or bore uncounted costs. A civilizational system that hopes to evolve must allow evidence to revise its account of its own superiority.
changes.rationale: Make the new empirical argument itself subject to measurement, comparison, alternative explanations, and revision.
